newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 26.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Fidel Ramos stays one more night at the Makati Medical Centre for more blood tests but says he will report for work at noon on Thursday. (ALL PAPERS)
- Senate president Ernesto Maceda says he expects a five-cornered fight for the presidential elections in 1998. (ALL PAPERS)
- Congressmen are insistent that they keep the countrywide development fund, the sore point stopping passage of the 1997 budget. (PHILIPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The Department of Trade and Industry is studying plans to reimpose taxes on exports of raw materials such as timber, coconut oil and other agricultural products. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- Two senators are asking the Energy Regulatory Board to stop raising petroleum prices on a monthly basis, saying it was disadvantageous to consumers. (BUSINESS DAILY)

- The Board of Investments has approved for registration and incentives a two billion peso power generation project of Southern Philippines Power Corp in General Santos city. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission has given the Manila International Futures Exchange until the end of the year to come up with concrete reform programmes. It said its licence would otherwise be revoked. (MANILA TIMES)
